overview.title: From customer pain to shipped AI product

products.name: AI Policy Foundry
products.tagline: Autonomous cloud-security policy from live threat intel and your own risk register.
products.summary: Generates cloud-security policy from the organisation's own risk register. Audit-ready in minutes, not weeks.
products.headline: Policy review cycles cut from 1–3 weeks to 30 minutes
products.pain: Cloud security policy is written by hand: 1–3 weeks per policy, 60–75% coverage. Providers ship new services faster than policy keeps up, so gaps (and risk) accumulate.
products.bet: A multi-agent system that generates, validates and continuously updates policy from live threat intel **and** the organisation's own uploaded risk/control docs.
products.whyLabel: Why AI is the right call
products.why: Inputs are unstructured (threat feeds, regulations, risk registers) and the mapping is non-deterministic. Templates can't do that; it needs language understanding and reasoning. Grounding in the organisation's own documents lifts accuracy from ~65% to ~95%.
products.tradeoff: Deprioritised multi-cloud breadth to first get per-clause traceability right. An auditor won't trust a policy they can't trace back to a specific control.
products.validated: BP's cloud-security policy-management team. Their weeks-long manual cycles and creeping coverage gaps drove risk-register grounding + continuous auto-update.
outcomes: Policy review cycles cut from 1–3 weeks to 30 minutes
95%+ policy accuracy and $2.4M annual savings
Roadmap: threat correlation, batch docs, OCR

products.name: AI SOC Portal
products.tagline: Auditable, AI-native SOC triage and threat hunting. Every verdict can be replayed.
products.summary: An AI-native SOC workspace where every machine verdict can be traced, evaluated and audited. Trust is a product requirement.
products.headline: Mean Time to Triage cut by more than 60%
products.pain: Most “AI for SOC” just wires an LLM to the alert queue. But a Tier-1 analyst won't act on a verdict they can't interrogate, and a CISO won't sign off on a control they can't evidence. Trust, not capability, blocks adoption.
products.bet: Agentic triage, threat hunting and incident response over live telemetry, built so every conclusion is replayable. ~Half the repo is reasoning, evaluation and audit infrastructure.
products.whyLabel: Why AI is the right call
products.why: Yes for triage, correlation and natural-language hunting, where LLM + RAG work well. But only when paired with an explainability, evaluation and audit layer. Raw AI alone is a non-starter in a regulated SOC.
products.tradeoff: Spent the build on trust infrastructure over more raw detection features. In a regulated SOC, trust is what gates adoption.
products.validated: Multiple interview rounds across all levels of BP's SOC team. Analysts won't act on a verdict they can't interrogate, so ~half the build is eval, explainability and audit.
outcomes: Mean Time to Triage cut by more than 60%; executive reporting overhead ~50% lower
85%+ analyst action rate at RAGAS groundedness above 0.90
Roadmap: SIEM/EDR ingest

products.name: AI Security Posture Management (AI-SPM)
products.tagline: Posture management for your own AI/ML assets, drift and compliance evidence.
products.summary: Governs and secures the organisation's own AI/ML assets across their lifecycle. Built with applied ML, not an LLM.
products.headline: Sub-second threat blocking; drift detection across 6 data quality dimensions
products.pain: Enterprises ship AI into production, but models, datasets, pipelines and endpoints are an unmanaged attack surface. There is no inventory, no adversarial detection and no drift monitoring, under rising NIST AI RMF / EU AI Act / GDPR pressure.
products.bet: Posture management for AI itself: inventory + lineage, adversarial-attack detection, data-quality & drift monitoring, and automated compliance evidence. One governed view for analyst, ML engineer, compliance and CISO.
products.why: Adversarial (FGSM/PGD/C&W), drift (KS, Chi-sq, Wasserstein) and anomaly (Isolation Forest/LOF/DBSCAN) problems are statistical, so the tooling is statistical too.
products.tradeoff: Chose applied ML/statistics over an LLM. An LLM would add cost and risk, not accuracy.
products.validated: BP's cloud-security team on how they plan to secure the org's AI initiatives. The absence of any AI-asset inventory scoped this to posture management for AI itself.
outcomes: Sub-second threat blocking; drift detection across 6 data quality dimensions
Automated compliance evidence, Wiz-native
Roadmap: broader frameworks & integrations

products.name: Exploit Validation & Remediation MCP Server
products.tagline: A governed MCP server for the validate → approve → remediate loop.
products.summary: A governed MCP bridge that lets AI agents run the validate → approve → remediate → re-verify loop, with a human approving each fix.
products.headline: Cuts mean-time-to-remediate
products.pain: Vulnerability management is a broken loop. An alert fires, but proving the CVE is exploitable, getting approval, patching and re-verifying happen manually across tools. And no one lets AI touch remediation without guardrails.
products.bet: A standard MCP server so a conversational AI can safely drive a closed-loop workflow. Engineers reach it from their chat and IDE.
products.whyLabel: Why AI is the right call
products.why: AI handles the natural-language request and the orchestration, turning “verify this CVE and patch if real” into safe, stateful tool calls. Validation & remediation stay deterministic; approval stays human. AI orchestrates, it doesn't decide.
products.tradeoff: Kept validation and remediation deterministic and left approval to a human. Deprioritised full autonomy so security teams can actually adopt it.
products.validated: Direct Qualys customer feedback asking to stay flexible across their own and 3rd-party tooling. That drove an open, standard MCP design over a closed, one-off integration.
outcomes: Extends the risk platform to safe AI agents
Cuts mean-time-to-remediate
Roadmap: live-API mode, deeper autonomy matrix

products.name: Unified Risk Copilot
products.tagline: Conversational risk triage across 8 security modules, fully audited.
products.summary: One conversation that joins 8 security modules into a ranked, evidence-backed, auditable remediation plan.
products.headline: Weekly risk report: hours → minutes
products.pain: Teams run 8+ modules (VM, WAS, PC, TotalCloud, Container, Cloud Agent, Patch, CSAM) in separate UIs. No single “what to fix first” view, the CISO's weekly report is a manual spreadsheet, and managers want data without write access.
products.bet: A “Weekly Risk Copilot” on the official MCP server: an LLM joins all 8 modules into one ranked narrative, with allow-listing, read-only mode, audit logging and approval-gated remediation built in.
products.whyLabel: Why AI is the right call
products.why: Cross-domain correlation, natural-language querying and report writing suit an LLM: the join logic is fuzzy and the output is prose. Governance is deterministic guardrails; remediation is human-approved.
products.tradeoff: Shipped read-only + approval-gated first. Deprioritised write/automation to earn trust before letting AI act across 8 modules.
products.validated: The same Qualys customer signal (stay flexible across the stack) led to wrapping the official MCP server, not building yet another siloed console.
outcomes: Weekly risk report: hours → minutes
Defensible, fully audited, safe self-service
Roadmap: live qualys-cli, more agent actions

products.name: HS Code Prediction API
products.tagline: Customs classification with classic ML, not an LLM.
products.summary: Predicts customs codes from a plain-text product description, using classic ML instead of an LLM.
products.headline: Accurate landed cost at checkout; less manual work
products.pain: Customs classification (assigning HS codes) is manual, slow and error-prone. A wrong code means fines, shipment delays and compliance risk, and trade teams still look codes up by hand, item by item.
products.bet: A production-shaped microservice that predicts an HS code from free text, with chapter / heading / subheading breakdown and confidence. Drops into a trade pipeline as a cheap-to-serve API.
products.why: This is a standard supervised text-classification task, so classic ML (TF-IDF + logistic regression) fits. It is lightweight, explainable and cheap. Matching model complexity to the problem is the product decision.
products.tradeoff: Shipped classic ML at ~55% rather than chase an LLM. For this buyer, a cheap, explainable, deployable pipeline mattered more than top accuracy.
products.validated: eBay's need to show an accurate total landed cost at checkout; validated with customs domain experts on how HS codes are really assigned.
outcomes: Accurate landed cost at checkout; less manual work
Ship-ready, cheap-to-serve ML packaging
Roadmap: transformer models, batch predict, caching

products.name: KYC-as-a-Service
products.tagline: Verifiable, privacy-preserving credit scoring, with AI on a blockchain.
products.summary: Verifiable, privacy-preserving credit-risk scoring: AI wrapped in blockchain provenance and federated learning.
products.headline: Adoptable AI scoring for regulated finance
products.pain: Banks need real-time, auditable credit-risk scores, but regulators distrust black-box AI scoring. And institutions can't pool data to improve models without exposing customer PII.
products.bet: A three-layer hybrid: blockchain as immutable source-of-truth & model provenance, off-chain AI for scoring, and a signed API. Federated learning lets institutions improve the model without sharing raw data.
products.why: Credit scoring on tabular/behavioural features is supervised ML, so GBM, not an LLM. The hard part is making the AI verifiable and private; those are the barriers, not the maths.
products.tradeoff: Invested in verifiability (blockchain) and privacy (federated learning) over model sophistication. Those were the real barriers to adoption.
products.validated: Western Union customers couldn't get credit in a new country without history or documents; KYC requirements validated with multiple financial institutions.
outcomes: Adoptable AI scoring for regulated finance
Multi-institution collaboration, GDPR-aware
Solves thin-file cold-start via shared learning
products.note: Status: targeted for launch in select markets.

products.name: Ellyra Pulse
products.tagline: Safety-gated patient sentiment for a medical AI: PHI-safe, clinical trust first.
products.summary: Safety-gated NPS and sentiment intelligence for a medical AI companion. Safety signals reach a clinician in minutes, not a weekly report.
products.headline: Safety-flagged detractors: 15-min SLA vs. 24h, with automatic clinical on-call paging
products.pain: One aggregate NPS hides three very different failures: a UI annoyance, a cold tone, or an AI answer that broke someone's trust in their own care. Verbatims routinely carry PHI, and a genuine safety miss (a misread decimal on a blood panel) sits in a weekly report instead of reaching a clinician in minutes.
products.bet: A feedback pipeline where a clinical risk gate runs before any survey fires, PHI is redacted before storage or any model call, and aspect-level sentiment separates detractor volume from detractor severity. Safety signals page clinical on-call instead of becoming one more dashboard row.
products.whyLabel: Why AI is the right call
products.why: Medical verbatims are unstructured and multi-aspect: “accurate, but felt cold” is two signals. Aspect-based sentiment across clinical trust, tone, OCR quality and actionability surfaces the rare, trust-breaking failures a theme-frequency count buries. Safety routing stays deterministic: models add evidence, never gate a P0.
products.tradeoff: Chose an auditable, rule-based safety gate over a smarter LLM classifier, and shipped schema, routing and dashboard before deeper analysis (SHAP drivers, root-cause quadrant). A clinician must be able to see exactly why a case was paged.
products.validated: Ellyra's clinical and product teams. An NPS score that can't tell a UI gripe from a broken-trust safety miss, plus PHI in free-text feedback, drove the pre-survey risk gate and redact-before-storage design.
outcomes: Safety-flagged detractors: 15-min SLA vs. 24h, with automatic clinical on-call paging
Targets: anxiety relief >75%, comprehension >85%, inaccuracy flags <0.2%
Roadmap: medical NER redaction, live UI-to-API wiring, SHAP driver analysis

ecosystem.title: The AI Defense Ecosystem.
ecosystem.subtitle: Three products, one platform, covering the full lifecycle. AI both defends the enterprise and is something the enterprise must defend.

pillars.text: Generate & maintain cloud-security policy from live intel + the org's risk register.

pillars.name: AI-SPM
pillars.text: Governs the org's own AI/ML assets: adversarial defense, drift, compliance evidence.

pillars.name: AI SOC Portal
pillars.text: Auditable, AI-native triage, hunting & response over live security telemetry.

ecosystem.spine: **One trust layer across all three.** Every AI decision is explainable, evaluated and logged. Gaps found in Detect feed back to Prevent; assets in Protect are watched by Detect.
opportunity: AI-security spend is growing but split across point tools. No one owns the whole lifecycle.
Regulation (EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF) requires every enterprise to govern its AI. That buyer need is mandatory and growing.
“AI as defender” and “AI as attack surface” treated as one problem. Few competitors frame it this way.
differentiator: Full-lifecycle coverage (prevent → protect → detect & respond) vs. single-point competitors.
Trust as a first-class product layer, grounded in the customer's own risk register and AI assets.
Agentic actions are governed and approved by a human, never an autonomous black box. Land in one pillar, expand across the loop.
